newsitem.title: ITALY: Norwegian explorer Ousland reaches South Pole.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian explorer Ousland reaches South Pole.

text.p: Norwegian explorer Borge Ousland has reached the South Pole, the halfway mark in his bid to trek 2,700 km (1,700 miles) across Antarctica alone and unsupported, his sponsor said on Friday.

"At 18:52 GMT yesterday, the Norwegian explorer...crossed the extreme southern latitude of the planet and now needs to go only 1,400 km more to complete his crossing," the sponsor said in a statement issued from its Milan public relations office.
Ousland set out on November 15 from Berkner Island in the Weddel Sea to try to walk across Antarctica to the Mcmurdo Base on Ross Island.
He reached the South Pole during a first attempt over the route last year, but frostbite forced him to give up after 44 days on the world's coldest continent.
"Compared to last year, his pace is exceptional: 35 days against 44...with a daily average of 38 km against 28.6 km," in 1995, the statement said.

It said Ousland was greeted at the South Pole by the people who work at the Scott-Amundsen base. "He stayed there for a few hours to take some photos and talk a bit after five weeks of absolute solitude," it said.
In last year's trek, Ousland was racing explorer Roger Mear to set a new endurance record, but the Briton also had to abandon his walk after vital equipment failed.
